node-1.label: Patient was admitted for evaluation of low-grade fever

node-2.label: A 55-year-old man had severe dilated cardiomyopathy and a left ventricular assist device (HeartMate II) implanted four years previously

node-3.label: Serum creatinine increased from 124 μmol/L to 354 μmol/L over two months; urinary protein excretion was 2.2 g/day with microhaematuria

why.why: All three expert analyses (laboratory, pathology, radiology) uniformly confirm active LVAD infection and infection-related GN: C. jeikeium bacteremia, FDG-PET/CT activity at driveline/pocket/outflow cannula, low C3, and immune-complex crescentic GN. The pathologist explicitly calls C. jeikeium LVAD infection causing infection-related GN the most credible diagnosis, and the radiologist confirms the immune-complex pattern fits infection-related GN. Although echocardiography is still missing, the available evidence is sufficient. Confidence is raised from 0.94 to 0.96.

Expert analyses specifically exclude primary ANCA-associated nephritis and emphasize that the immune-complex pattern, low C3, and active LVAD infection all point to infection-related GN rather than primary glomerulonephritis. Confidence is lowered from 0.05 to 0.04.

The pathologist explicitly states mechanical renal injury is essentially excluded; the immune-complex crescentic GN and active infection on PET/CT are not explained by mechanical device injury. Confidence is lowered from 0.02 to 0.01.

node-8.label: Blood cultures were positive for Corynebacterium jeikeium

node-10.label: Renal biopsy showed mesangial IgM/C1q/C3 deposits without subepithelial humps

node-11.label: Renal biopsy showed focal segmental necrotising immune-complex glomerulonephritis with crescents

node-12.label: PR3-ANCA was elevated and MPO-ANCA was negative

node-13.label: Corynebacterium jeikeium LVAD infection causing infection-related glomerulonephritis

why.why: Pathologist analysis states this named-organism causal diagnosis is the most credible, supported by positive C. jeikeium blood cultures, PET/CT activity at driveline/pocket/outflow cannula, low C3, and mesangial immune-complex deposits without humps. Radiologist also confirms active infection and immune-complex GN with crescents. Confidence is raised from 0.92 to 0.95.

node-14.label: LVAD infection-related immune-complex glomerulonephritis with crescents

why.why: Radiologist and pathologist analyses emphasize the biopsy shows mesangial/subendothelial immune-complex deposits without humps and crescentic GN, with low C3, fitting infection-related immune-complex GN with crescents. Expert consensus strengthens this refined hypothesis. Confidence is raised from 0.88 to 0.90.

Experts interpret the elevated PR3-ANCA as a secondary phenomenon of chronic C. jeikeium infection rather than evidence of true ANCA-associated GN; the immune-complex pattern and low C3 favor infection-related immune-complex GN. Thus LVAD infection-associated secondary PR3-ANCA glomerulonephritis remains unlikely. Confidence is lowered from 0.15 to 0.10.

node-16.label: FDG-PET/CT shows increased FDG activity at the driveline, pocket, and outflow cannula

node-18.label: Renal biopsy showed subendothelial and mesangial immune-complex deposits

node-3.label: Serum creatinine increased from 124 μmol/L to 354 μmol/L over two months; urinary protein excretion was 2.2 g/day with microhaematuria

why.why: All three expert analyses (laboratory, pathology, radiology) uniformly confirm active LVAD infection and infection-related GN: C. jeikeium bacteremia, FDG-PET/CT activity at driveline/pocket/outflow cannula, low C3, and immune-complex crescentic GN. The pathologist explicitly calls C. jeikeium LVAD infection causing infection-related GN the most credible diagnosis, and the radiologist confirms the immune-complex pattern fits infection-related GN. Although echocardiography is still missing, the available evidence is sufficient. Confidence is raised from 0.94 to 0.96.

Expert analyses specifically exclude primary ANCA-associated nephritis and emphasize that the immune-complex pattern, low C3, and active LVAD infection all point to infection-related GN rather than primary glomerulonephritis. Confidence is lowered from 0.05 to 0.04.

The pathologist explicitly states mechanical renal injury is essentially excluded; the immune-complex crescentic GN and active infection on PET/CT are not explained by mechanical device injury. Confidence is lowered from 0.02 to 0.01.

node-8.label: Blood cultures were positive for Corynebacterium jeikeium

node-10.label: Renal biopsy showed mesangial IgM/C1q/C3 deposits without subepithelial humps

node-11.label: Renal biopsy showed focal segmental necrotising immune-complex glomerulonephritis with crescents

node-12.label: PR3-ANCA was elevated and MPO-ANCA was negative

node-13.label: Corynebacterium jeikeium LVAD infection causing infection-related glomerulonephritis

why.why: Pathologist analysis states this named-organism causal diagnosis is the most credible, supported by positive C. jeikeium blood cultures, PET/CT activity at driveline/pocket/outflow cannula, low C3, and mesangial immune-complex deposits without humps. Radiologist also confirms active infection and immune-complex GN with crescents. Confidence is raised from 0.92 to 0.95.

node-14.label: LVAD infection-related immune-complex glomerulonephritis with crescents

why.why: Radiologist and pathologist analyses emphasize the biopsy shows mesangial/subendothelial immune-complex deposits without humps and crescentic GN, with low C3, fitting infection-related immune-complex GN with crescents. Expert consensus strengthens this refined hypothesis. Confidence is raised from 0.88 to 0.90.

Experts interpret the elevated PR3-ANCA as a secondary phenomenon of chronic C. jeikeium infection rather than evidence of true ANCA-associated GN; the immune-complex pattern and low C3 favor infection-related immune-complex GN. Thus LVAD infection-associated secondary PR3-ANCA glomerulonephritis remains unlikely. Confidence is lowered from 0.15 to 0.10.

node-16.label: FDG-PET/CT shows increased FDG activity at the driveline, pocket, and outflow cannula

node-17.label: Active Corynebacterium jeikeium LVAD infection involving the driveline, pocket, and outflow cannula

why.why: Expert analyses uniformly confirm active LVAD infection: FDG-PET/CT shows increased activity at the driveline, pocket, and outflow cannula, and blood cultures grew C. jeikeium. The pathologist states the LVAD infection diagnosis is clear, and the radiologist confirms active infection. Confidence is raised from 0.92 to 0.95.

node-18.label: Renal biopsy showed subendothelial and mesangial immune-complex deposits

attrs.why: PR3-ANCA is elevated and MPO-ANCA is negative, which initially raised concern for ANCA-associated GN; however, expert analyses interpret the ANCA elevation as a secondary phenomenon of chronic C. jeikeium infection, and the biopsy shows immune-complex deposits with low C3, making primary ANCA-associated GN very unlikely. Confidence is 0.03.
